info.title: GraySpace Terrain API
info.description:
What the simulated internet offers and how it is doing, and the enclaves built at its edge: the
deployed core version, its inventory (routers, links and core services with their addresses and status)
and DNS (every zone and record), shipped versions and their snapshots, capabilities, attachment points, enclaves,
instances and their manifests, jobs, images and roles, the CA bundle and the map layer. The core itself is deployed,
configured and destroyed through the API too.

One GraySpace runs several deployments, each a core and the enclaves on it. `GET /api/v1/deployments` lists them;
every other route is a deployment's, under its base URL `/deployments/{deployment}` (so the core is
`/deployments/abc/api/v1/base`). Without the prefix, a route reaches the default deployment: that alias is
deprecated. A client such as GHOSTS takes the deployment's base URL as its GraySpace address.

Every route needs a bearer token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: the server's service token
(`GRAYSPACE_API_TOKEN`), which may do everything, or a person's session token from `POST /api/v1/auth/login`.
A person sees only the deployments they own or are a member of (others are 404), and may only do what their
access there allows (403 otherwise): `GET /api/v1/me` gives their role, and each deployment's `my_access`
what they may do in it.
Live updates come over the deployment's `/api/v1/events` websocket (`grayspace-events-v1.json`); deployments
being created, changed and removed over `/api/v1/deployments/events` (`grayspace-deployments-events-v1.json`).

**From nothing deployed to a core and a slice** (paths relative to the deployment's base URL):

0. `POST /api/v1/deployments` with `{"id": "abd"}` (at the server's root), unless the deployment exists. It runs on the
   default Proxmox connection; `placement` chooses another, or another node (`GET /api/v1/platform`).
1. `GET /api/v1/base/preflight?version=grayspace/2026.11&scope=tier1`: is the site ready? Fix every `error`.
2. `POST /api/v1/base/deploy` with `{"version": "grayspace/2026.11", "scope": "tier1"}`: returns a job.
3. `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}` (or its streamed `/log`, or `/events`) until it succeeds; then `GET /api/v1/base` is `healthy`.
4. `PUT /api/v1/enclaves/{slug}` with an enclave spec (`grayspace-enclave-v1.json`); fix any error findings.
5. `POST /api/v1/instances` with `{"enclave": "<slug>"}`: returns a job; when it succeeds, `GET /api/v1/instances/{id}` is the manifest.

Or in one job: `PUT /api/v1/draft` with the core and the enclave instances the deployment should have
(`{"base": {"version": "grayspace/2026.11", "scope": "tier1"}, "enclaves": [{"slug": "<slug>", "prefix": "bk"}]}`),
`GET /api/v1/deploy/plan` to see what would change, then `POST /api/v1/deploy`: a rollout job that destroys what the
draft no longer has, deploys or updates the core, and creates the instances, each as a child job (`GET /api/v1/jobs?parent={id}`).
Change the draft and deploy again to change the deployment. Since 1.8 the draft's core may name a
preset (`preset`), a saved set of runtime changes the rollout applies once the core is built. Since 1.10
the draft's `player` is the deployment's Crucible Player view: its applications, teams, and which core and enclave VMs
each team sees (`GET /api/v1/player/guests`); the rollout applies it last, in its `player` stage.
Since 1.11 a Proxmox connection may set `apply_parallelism` and `plan_parallelism`, Terraform's parallelism for the
deployments placed on it (applies and destroys: how many guests are created at once; plans).
Since 1.12 a deployment's `options.use_custom_image` is deprecated and ignored: every deployment's Alpine guests use
the GraySpace image.
Since 1.13 the core has no `grafana` guest (the web app has the dashboards): `GET /api/v1/player/guests` no longer
lists it, and a draft's Player guest that names it is dropped (since 1.17 without a warning, when the draft is read or saved).
Since 1.14 `GET /api/v1/player` has the view's `url` in Player's UI.
Since 1.15 the draft's `player.assign` gives every guest of the core or of an enclave instance to teams; `player.guests`
lists the guests whose teams differ.
Since 1.16 `GET /api/v1/base/preview` is a shipped version's map before it is deployed, and a Crucible connection may
set `player_url`, Player's UI when it isn't the Player API URL without /api.
Since 1.18 the core has no clients: a core version is ISPs, routers, links, DNS servers and CAs, and hosts on the
simulated internet are enclaves (`grayspace/2026.11`; `grayspace/2026.10` is retired). The inventory's `clients`, a
version summary's `clients` and the capabilities' `host_features` are deprecated and always empty or 0, `guest.update`
no longer comes for a `client`, and `client.move` is no longer a core action (a preset that has one lists it in its
`problems`), and a draft's Player guest that names one is dropped without a warning. An image with the `desktop`
feature (`grayspace-desktop`) is a desktop in the browser.
Since 1.19 enclaves have no presets: an enclave is what its spec builds, and a variant is another enclave. The routes
`/api/v1/enclaves/{slug}/presets` and `/api/v1/instances/{id}/presets` are gone, a draft's `enclaves[].preset` is
deprecated and ignored, an instance and a planned instance no longer have `preset` and `active_preset`, and the plan has
no `preset:<id>` stages. An instance's actions are live changes its reset undoes. Core presets are unchanged.
Since 1.20 `POST /api/v1/enclaves/{slug}/validate` takes `instance`, a draft's prefix, to check the spec as that
instance: when it is live and built from the enclave, its prefix, DNS names and links are its own, not conflicts.
Since 1.21 a role can name the image types it runs on (`image_types`, e.g. `[vm]` for `ad-dc`), and a host whose image
is another type gets `INCOMPATIBLE_ROLE`.
Since 1.22 a rollout resumes only while the draft is the one it deployed: after the draft changes, retrying it is refused
(409; deploy instead), and `GET /api/v1/deploy/plan` has `resumable_rollout`, the last rollout when it can still be
retried. A destroyed instance is no longer managed by the draft, however it was destroyed.
Since 1.23 a Proxmox connection chooses the proxy its deployments' guests install packages through (`proxy_mode`: `site`,
the site file's, by default; `none`; or `custom`, with `proxy` and `no_proxy`).
Since 1.24 the hosts of a site with a domain controller (an `ad-dc` host) use it as their resolver (an allocated host's
`resolver`); the DC keeps the core resolver, its DNS's forwarder. A site's `resolver` is still the core's.
Since 1.25 the core has no GHOSTS VM: enclave hosts run GHOSTS clients (the `ghosts-client` role), which report to a
GHOSTS server outside the simulated internet. A deployment's `options.deploy_ghosts` is deprecated and ignored,
`GET /api/v1/player/guests` no longer lists `ghosts`, a draft's Player guest that names it is dropped without a warning,
and the core preflight has no `ghosts-vm` check.

Tear down in reverse: `DELETE /api/v1/instances/{id}`, then `DELETE /api/v1/base`. Long-running work is always a
job: poll it, read its log, cancel it, or retry it from the stage that failed.

servers.description: The default deployment. Deprecated: name the deployment

get.description:
The deployed core version and its health.

The version comes from the `base` block that `task parse` writes into terraform.tfvars.json.
Health compares the routers in the tfvars with what Proxmox reports as running, and counts
BGP sessions up across all routers from Prometheus.

delete.description:
Destroy the core (task destroy). Refused while slice instances are live, unless
destroy_instances is true: then each live instance's destroy job is queued first, and the
core's destroy job last, which refuses to run if any instance is still live. Returns the jobs
in the order they run; the last is the core's.

parameters.name: destroy_instances

schema.description: Destroy every live slice instance first
schema.title: Destroy Instances

parameters.description: Destroy every live slice instance first

schema.title: Response Destroy Base Api V1 Base Delete

409.description: Live instances exist (pass destroy_instances=true), or another job is active

get.description:
What the deployed core consists of: ISPs; routers with their interfaces and addresses; links
with both ends' addresses and their state; clients (the hosts the core places on customer
networks) and core services (DNS servers and CAs) with their addresses. Read from the deployed
tfvars, so only what the deployment scope built. Status is Proxmox's, link state comes from
Prometheus. Slice instances are not included: GET /instances/{id} returns each one's manifest.

Every zone the simulated DNS serves and its records (all but the SOA), with the resolvers.
Each zone and record has an origin: `base` (the root and TLD zones task configure writes),
`overlay` (domains and records created in the web UI or by a core preset) or `instance` (created by a
slice instance, named in `instance`). Delegations sit in their TLD zone with the origin of the
domain they delegate.

Shipped core versions under bases/, with a summary of each and which one is deployed.

A version whose CSVs fail to load is listed with its problems instead of a summary.

schema.title: Response List Base Versions Api V1 Base Versions Get

get.description:
A core version and its topology snapshot: ISPs, locations, routers (with ISP and location)
and links. Version names contain a slash, e.g. /api/v1/base/versions/grayspace/2026.11.

Whether this site can deploy the core version at the scope: the settings, the Proxmox API and
node, storages (and their content types), bridges, SDN, SSH to the Proxmox host, capacity, and
live instances that a version change would break. A deploy is refused while any check is an
error, and runs these again as its first stage.

parameters.name: version

schema.description: Core version to check; the deployed one by default
schema.title: Version

parameters.description: Core version to check; the deployed one by default

parameters.name: scope

schema.description: full or tier1; the deployed scope, else full
schema.title: Scope

parameters.description: full or tier1; the deployed scope, else full

post.description:
Deploy or update the core: preflight, parse, the guards, Terraform until converged, Ansible,
then a health check that waits for routers and BGP. Returns a job; poll GET /jobs/{id} or follow
/events, then GET /base. Deploying the deployed version again changes nothing. Without a
version, the deployed one is redeployed; with nothing deployed, a version is required.

409.description: Another core job is queued or running, or live instances would break

422.description: Preflight failed; detail.checks lists the errors

post.description: Run Ansible on the deployed core again (task configure), then the health check. Returns a job.

409.description: Nothing is deployed, or another core job is queued or running

get.description:
The saved draft. Before anyone saves one, a draft of what is deployed (adopted: true), whose
instances the draft then manages; instances GHOSTS owns are left out.

put.description: Save what the deployment should have. Nothing changes until POST /deploy.

422.description: An unknown core version or enclave, or a prefix used twice

get.description:
What POST /deploy would do: instances to destroy, the core to deploy or update, instances to
create, and the node's capacity now. problems lists what stops it.

post.description:
Queue a rollout: destroys, then the core, then creates, each a child job, stopping at the first
that fails. Poll GET /jobs/{id} (its children, and GET /jobs?parent={id}); retry it to resume.

409.description: Nothing to change, a core job or rollout is active, or the plan has problems

delete.description:
A destroy job: revoke certificates, delete DNS records and domains, undo link conditions and BGP
attachments, terraform destroy, delete the workspace, free the allocations. Allowed from any
state, including a failed create; a create still queued or running is cancelled first.

post.description:
A runtime action on a ready instance: link.condition, link.clear, link.down, link.up
on core links; dns.record.set and dns.record.delete within the instance's domains; host.start and
host.stop; reset, which undoes the instance's actions. Owned by the instance: Reset changes
(POST /changes/discard) leaves them, reset and destroy undo them.

409.description: The instance isn't ready, or another owner holds the link (LINK_OWNED)

post.description: Cancel: interrupt the command the job is running (Terraform stops gracefully), or stop at the next stage boundary. A create that is cancelled leaves the instance failed, to be retried or destroyed.

city), links (great-circle LineStrings, split at the 180° meridian), and slice sites, internet
hosts and their attachments. Colors and states are properties, so every map draws the same
thing; updates arrive by feature id over /api/v1/events (feature.update) and /ws.

post.description:
Create a deployment: its directory, environment file and work tree, and start its worker.
You become its owner. Its Terrain API is then at /deployments/{id}/api/v1; deploy its core with
POST /deployments/{id}/api/v1/base/deploy.

403.description: Only builders and admins create deployments

patch.description:
name and description change any time; placement (a connection and node), options and
router_password only while nothing is deployed, and the worker restarts with them (owners and
admins). default: admins. proxmox and credentials are the connection's: refused.

delete.description:
Remove a deployment that has nothing deployed. A managed deployment's directory is deleted;
an adopted tree is only forgotten. Owners and admins.

put.description:
Who else may see and use the deployment: build access (builders only) or use access.
Replaces the list. Owners and admins.

422.description: An unknown user, the owner, or build access for a user

post.description:
Restart the deployment's worker. A managed deployment's work tree is refreshed from the
server's code first. Jobs running in it fail, as on any backend restart. Needs build.
A session for a local account. Send its token as Authorization: Bearer <token>.
